features.title: The profile rules table
features.description: audit-profile.mjs: PROFILES, QUICK_SUBSYSTEM_REF, QUICK_DEFERRED, profileRules(profile) and the tolerant rulesOf(meta); audit-run.mjs takes KNOWN_PROFILES and REASONS.quick from it. The dry run: pure code, read against upstream.
acceptance: audit-profile.mjs exports PROFILES (quick, standard, deep, frozen), QUICK_SUBSYSTEM_REF and QUICK_DEFERRED with upstream's exact strings
profileRules returns the frozen row of the contract table for each profile and throws a TypeError naming the value for anything that is not exactly a profile name
rulesOf(meta) returns the run's rules, and standard for a meta with no profile, an unknown one, null or undefined; profileRules's TypeError says exactly `unknown profile <value as JSON>`
the table agrees with criticReserve, validationReserve, KNOWN_PROFILES and REASONS.quick, which already exist
every rule is backed by upstream's vendored text, read by the test

features.title: init takes quick and deep
features.description: audit-run.mjs init --profile quick|deep starts a run behind the existing gates; SUPPORTED_PROFILES is all three; check, status and next work on them; usage text, comments and the what-runs note say so.
acceptance: SUPPORTED_PROFILES equals KNOWN_PROFILES: quick, standard, deep
init --profile quick and --profile deep print AUDIT: OK with the profile, record it, and the run passes check, status and next (NEXT: recon)
init with no profile is standard; a name that is not exactly one of the three is a usage error (exit 2) that creates nothing
the usage text names [--profile quick|standard|deep]
--budget 7 (quick) and 9 (deep and standard) are refused with upstream's reason and the calls the profile needs first, the run recorded incomplete; 8, 10 and 10 are accepted
the what-runs note says one verifier per surviving lead for quick, one or two for the others
check names the three profiles when a run's metadata holds anything else

features.title: The units a profile asks for
features.description: Quick seed and mint refuse any unit whose subsystem reference is not the fixed one or that carries a lifecycle (an earlier run's units are exempt); quick and deep stage inputs and prompts carry upstream's "Run profiles and scope" section verbatim; standard is untouched.
acceptance: a quick seed accepts units with subsystem reference profile/quick/all-in-scope-subsystems (labels free) and the ledger passes the vendored validator
a quick seed refuses any other subsystem reference and any lifecycle (label, reference or both), with the contract's messages, writing nothing and saving no step; seedProblems says the same
unitFromInput judges by ctx.profile, and a ctx with no profile is judged as before
standard and deep accept any subsystem reference and lifecycle units (an ID ends in the mode)
a unit an earlier run held is still force-added to a quick ledger with its own references

for quick and deep, parts.profile of the synthesizer, critic and minter inputs is the vendored section byte for byte and each prompt carries it verbatim under its heading; for standard there is no such key and no such text

features.title: Quick's one wave and one critic
features.description: nextStep sends a quick run from apply-critic to validation (no second wave, no final-clean critic); apply-critic defers what the critic found, what it reopened and every unit no hunter reached, with quick_profile_final_critic.
acceptance: nextStep: quick goes from apply-critic to validation whatever planned units remain; standard, deep and a meta with no profile go on hunting or to the final-clean critic as before
a quick run with nothing huntable, or whose wave the budget deferred whole, still gets its one critic, kind post-wave; standard asks the final-clean critic

apply-critic in quick: reopened units are archived and deferred (wave + 1, no owner, no evidence, reason quick_profile_final_critic), minted units and units no hunter reached are deferred with the same reason, candidates stay, nothing is left planned; the ledger passes the validator and next says validate
apply-critic in quick ends with deferred=<count> in its summary; standard and deep have no such field
a unit a verifier owns (a carried prior record) stays planned in quick and the run goes to validation
in a scoped quick run a minted unit outside the scope is out_of_scope, not deferred
a quick minted unit must be coarsened too: refused with the seed's message and counted as rejected
plan-wave is refused after a quick critic result is applied; standard and deep are unchanged

features.title: Quick merges Phase 3 and Phase 5
features.description: The validate stage of a quick run carries upstream's Phase 5 checks and marks each decided lead merged; next skips verify; write-findings ends the run; complete-check accepts the marker in quick only, for the entry's own Phase 3 verifier only.
acceptance: for quick, the validate input has parts.phase5 (the vendored Phase 5 section, byte for byte) and each verifier prompt carries it, says it is merged into this pass and that there is no later Phase 5 pass; standard and deep have neither
each decided needs_validation entry of a quick run gets phase5 { state: merged, verifier_id: its own v verifier }; a rejected entry stays null
nextStep after write-findings is report for quick and verify (when a record needs it) for standard and deep
write-findings in a quick run ends the run complete; complete-check finds nothing; check passes
a quick record with a wrong, missing or verified-state marker makes the run incomplete (complete_check_failed) without a throw
a retried candidate is marked with the verifier whose result was kept; the marker naming the discarded attempt fails complete-check
the validate stage funds floor(left / verifiersPerCandidate) candidates: quick two with two agents left, standard and deep one and incomplete (validation_budget_exhausted)
in standard and deep a merged marker does not satisfy complete-check, and verify is still its own stage

features.title: Deep's second pass
features.description: apply-critic in a deep run archives a prior_covered_same_source unit this run covered and plans it again for a fresh owner, once, with the contract's reason; everything else of deep is standard's.
acceptance: in deep, the first critic application after a prior_covered_same_source unit is covered archives its pass in attempts with the exact reassignment_reason, sets it planned at wave + 1 with no owner and no evidence, and next says plan-wave
a unit an earlier run did not cover is left alone; the ledger passes the validator
the next wave hunts only that unit, with a fresh owner (h2-01); a second critic application leaves it alone (second_pass=0) and the run goes to the final-clean critic
a unit the critic itself reopens in the same application is not archived twice; a prior same-source unit that came back a candidate or blocked gets no second pass
standard and quick do no second pass and have no second_pass field; deep's summary ends with second_pass=<count>
nextStep is the same line for deep as for standard in every stage-state fixture, and after write-findings deep goes to verify

features.title: What the report says about the profile
features.description: REPORT.md: a Profile rules line for quick and deep; partial pass for quick only (deep is not partial because of its profile); the one-critic sentence; a count of units deferred as quick_profile_final_critic.
acceptance: the Run section has the contract's exact Profile rules line for quick and for deep and none for standard
a complete quick run is a partial pass with the existing sentence; a complete deep or standard run under no scope or budget is not
scope, strict budget, deferred coverage and incompleteness are partial-pass reasons for every profile, in the existing order, and never a profile reason for deep
the Status of a complete quick run says its records passed the quick profile's merged Phase 3 and Phase 5 verification; standard and deep keep their sentence
a quick run's final critic section says its one critic was final by design; standard and deep keep their sentences

units deferred as quick_profile_final_critic are listed and counted in the contract's one sentence (deferred units whose reason is exactly that string, nothing a hunter wrote), placed after the gap list, and no such sentence appears without any

features.title: The docs
features.description: SKILL.md, the graph README and audit-run.mjs's own text name the three profiles, their rules and their minimum budgets (the code's numbers), and nothing says init refuses quick or deep.
acceptance: SKILL.md usage block is [--profile quick|standard|deep] and its flags still equal INIT_FLAGS plus --unattended and --guidance
SKILL.md and the README each list quick, standard and deep with the contract's phrases and the budget sentence with minimumBudget(profile), and say each profile keeps the same evidence bar
the skill's not-supported bullet and closing rule, the README status paragraph and audit-run.mjs's comments, usage and refusal no longer say quick or deep are refused or later
SKILL.md tells the session that a quick run is a partial pass
the existing tests (audit-skill, audit-readme as edited, validate.sh pins) still pass

features.title: End to end, quick
features.description: A whole offline quick audit of the toy repository from init --profile quick to the reports, driven by the skill's own commands: one wave, one critic, one verifier per lead, deferred gaps, a partial-pass report.
acceptance: the run is quick, complete, and its path is recon, seed, one wave, one critic and minter, apply-critic, consolidate, validate, write-findings, report with no verify and no final-clean critic
13 agents: one hunter for the four coarse units, one critic, one minter, one grouping, one v verifier per candidate
six units: four candidates, two deferred as quick_profile_final_critic, all under the fixed subsystem reference; both validators and check pass
three needs_validation leads and one rejected claim, each lead marked merged by its own v verifier, nothing confirmed
REPORT.md says quick: the rules line, a partial pass, the deferred count, the one critic by design, the merged verification; the audited repository is untouched
under --budget 13 (exactly what it spends) the quick run completes with 13 agents; under 12 it ends incomplete with validation_budget_exhausted and never spends past 12

features.title: End to end, deep
features.description: A whole offline deep audit of the toy repository from init --profile deep to the reports: standard's machine and agent count, a lifecycle unit, Phase 5 by separate verifiers, no partial pass.
acceptance: the run is deep, complete, and its path and its 22 agents are standard's
seven units including one lifecycle: delete unit with its own coverage ID, hunted with its subsystem; nothing deferred; both validators and check pass
each lead has a Phase 5 verifier (r) different from its Phase 3 verifier (v); nothing is marked merged
REPORT.md says deep, is not a partial pass, and still says complete, source only and not clean

a second deep audit of the same commit archives one second pass on each unit the first run covered (src/server.js#server, src/auth.js#currentUser): wave 2, an h2 owner, the contract's reason; nothing else is reopened
